messages:
maya: thinking aloud 1 - rather than stuffing compatibility logic into the runtime, what about a tiny "edge-guard" in the gateway that classifies and redirects incompatible payloads to a compat service for normalization. keeps runtime minimal and lets us iterate rules quickly.
jordan: latency concern. gateway is hot path. per-request classification + network hop could add to p50/p99.
priya: maybe make the classification super cheap: header probes + shape hints. only escalate to the compat service when heuristics indicate mismatch.
alex: agree. also want tenant-level opt-in for any automated rewrites so we can offer customers control.
maya: sketch of flow: gateway -> lightweight sniff -> cache check for rule -> if hit and rule.action == "rewrite" route to compat-service -> compat returns normalized request -> gateway forwards. else forward straight to runtime.
jordan: where do rules live? baked into gateway config is fastest but painful to update. central rules service with watch + TTL cache in gateway would be nicer.
priya: central rule service + streaming push (like config-stream) and a local cache in gateway. fallback to last-known rules if stream flaps.
sam: product ask: need auditability. support must see what rewrites happened and why. we also need a per-tenant opt-out and a way to request strict validation.
alex: add header X-Compat-Action: rewritten|passthrough and X-Compat-Rule: <rule-id>. emit as spans and logs. Console can surface recent rewrites per tenant.
maya: scaling: typical migrations we expect <1% traffic to hit compat-service, but spikes possible. compat-service must autoscale and be architected for short-lived stateless rewrites.
jordan: runtime fallback: if compat-service times out or errors, runtime should be capable of accepting legacy shapes via a lightweight adapter for a short window. double fallback reduces outage risk.
priya: time budgets idea: sniff <= 10ms, gateway wait for compat <= 80ms, compat target rewrite <= 30ms. if timeout, gateway marks tenant for runtime-adapter fast-path for N seconds and emits SLO alert.
maya: proto example (pseudo):
```
rule_id: "embed_dim_legacy_v1"
match {
  header_contains: "X-Client-Proto: 1"
  json_probe: "requests[*].embedding.length == 512"
}
action: "rewrite"
rewrite_template: "normalize_embeds_v2"
```
jordan: don't rely solely on client-version strings; prefer explicit feature headers when SDKs can set them. but we need heuristics for unupdated clients.
sam: support UX: Console needs a "compat activity" timeline (recent rewrites, rule ids, impacted tenants) and a one-click contact step to reach customers.
alex: telemetry: rule_match_count, rewrite_success_rate, rewrite_latency_histogram, per-tenant rewrite_percentage. console should alert if rewrite_rate > 5% or if rewrite_error_rate > 1%.
priya: security note: compat-service must enforce auth propagation and validate that it doesn't escalate privileges. run it in the same VPC and reuse gateway auth tokens.
jordan: implementation steps: 1) rule schema RFC, 2) central rules service + streaming, 3) gateway sniff + cache, 4) compat-service + short-lived runtime-adapter, 5) telemetry + console hooks, 6) canary rollout.
maya: canary plan: internal tenants -> 1% external sample -> region-limited -> progressive scale. use feature flags to control per-rule rollout.
sam: operations runbook items:
- If a rule causes > p99 latency regressions: flip rule to log-only sampling, notify customers.
- If compat-service fails: enable runtime-adapter fallback and rollback rule deployment.
- If rewrite correctness uncertain: run A/B sampling (rewrite vs passthrough) and compare outputs.
alex: tradeoff: adds components and failure modes vs easier iteration and hotfixes. leaning to edge-guard + compat-service for faster ops and rollouts.
jordan: agreed, but we must harden timeouts and fallbacks to avoid P0s.
maya: action items:
- @priya: draft rule schema + central-rule RFC (due EOW)
- @jordan: prototype runtime-adapter fallback behavior (next sprint)
- @alex: telemetry + console mockups for compat metrics (next week)
- @sam: support flow + message templates for customers (EOW)

deploy-bot: scheduled job created -> job/compat-edge-guard-canary #8472
maya: thanks all, will schedule RFC review next Tue. :rocket:
